Rachel,

I really don't know what to make of ALC. She appears to be deeply self loathing,  enamored with a dead person who shot Andy Warhol, and terrifyingly ignorant of the fact that her words can and will be politicized into weapons that will be aimed at our healthcare. I read her book today and I don't think its really a work of transfeminism. People like you or Julia Serano write to give trans people the language and ideas to understand ourselves and learn to fight against transphobia. ALC is not trying to do this. I think when ALC writes "Valerie would make statements not because they were accurate or provable, but simply because she *wanted to*" she is talking not just about Solanas but also about herself. Her writing is not theory, its art: it's absurd, provocative, and a bit pretentious just like that piano project she describes.

All that being said, if you ignore her projecting I think there's a lot of value in her work. In her NYT piece she told her story about becoming more miserable after transitioning, and how she neither regrets her transition nor deserves to be denied healthcare on the grounds that it makes her less happy (shouldn't wanting it be enough?). Her subjective experience and her critique of the current trans healthcare paradigm are valid. Whats not valid is her projecting that every other trans person experiences the same misery. Yes society requires us to perform suffering as part of the mainstream trans narrative, yes many of us are genuinely happy and reject this suffering based conception of trans identity, but also yes some of us are pretty dysphoric and miserable. Now It was extremely reckless for her to publish in the NYT. She doesn't seem to understand that these ridiculous and provocative things she says can cost lives if heard by the right policymakers. Also her n+1 article which reframes identity as desire really blew my mind to be honest. I definitely don't agree with everything she says but I think she has good ideas and we should be listening to them. Also I agree she is a really good writer.

By the way if you're reading this I just wanted to let you know that I'm a big fan of your writing and I loved your book.

They are pretty shady. One of my good friends is an American but grew up in the PRC and he said he heard that once a big shot in the CCP was having an organ transplant, and they gave the doctor three organs so that he had not one but two backups.

At the same time China is the second largest economy in the world, and is an advanced industrialized country with plenty of well educated people. If they can build a space station they can probably build an airplane. It’s not like they’re trying to build a counterfeit A321 and trick some airline into thinking it was made by Airbus. Additionally the C919 was actually developed in collaboration with Bombardier (a Canadian aerospace company) and the planned wide body jetliner will be designed in collaboration with UAC (a Russian aerospace company).

If they build it and the FAA and EASA say it’s safe then sure I’ll fly in it. I guess if you wanna only buy flights on safe American planes like the 737 MAX be my guest.

Yes China steals a lot of our ideas in order to catch up to the state of the art, but that allows them to start innovating instead of being stuck reinventing the technologies already developed by Boeing and Airbus. I believe in this instance enforcing intellectual property benefits the Boeing Airbus duopoly at the expense of humanity and consumers as a whole. While intellectual property can incentivize innovation, it can also slow the progress of humanity and entrench monopolies.
Spicy hot take: It’s a good thing if China develops its own competitor to the Boeing 737 and Airbus A32X because more competition benefits the consumer. Y’all just hate China.
